newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Ice locks Dutch canals, Rhine still clear.
newsitem.headline: Ice locks Dutch canals, Rhine still clear.

text.p: The continuing freeze in continental Europe has rendered key Dutch inland canals almost unnavigable, although the Rhine remains clear, Dutch water inspectors RIZA said on Monday.
Inland connections from Rotterdam to the south and into Belgium were hardest hit. All routes were blocked, making passage only possible by sea.
"There's very heavy floating ice. It's almost 100 percent covered. There's no possibility to go through," said a RIZA spokesman, referring to Rotterdam connections with Flushing and Antwerp.
He said there were no reports yet of blockages in southern coastal waters, but said that the low temperatures were made it increasingly hard to pass through the sea.
To the north, the Amsterdam-Rotterdam link was only just navigable, while icebreakers were keeping open supply routes through the IJsselmeer, the Dutch inland sea.
"There's heavy floating ice between Amsterdam and the Lek (river at Rotterdam). It's very difficult to get ships through," the RIZA spokesman said.
The Rhine, the main artery into western and southern Germany, remains free of major ice cover.
"The Rhine is still clear, with no floating ice," the RIZA spokesman said.
However, gates used to control the Rhine water level were being removed because of ice. The RIZA spokesman said the water level had fallen as a result.
Oil traders dealing in barges along the Rhine said the river remained open throughout Germany, but there were isolated troublespots.
"The Rhine is free, but Frankfurt is a bit tricky. Barge owners are asking a risk premium for some destinations," one trader said.
Some traders said they were nervous about chartering barges into parts of Germany. If the vessels become stuck, the traders are liable to additional barging costs.
On Friday, barge operators were not quoting freight rates for the Rotterdam-Dortmund route as ice had rendered Dortmund inaccessible.

Temperatures in most parts of the Netherlands reached -10 degrees Celsius (five degrees Fahrenheit) at the weekend. In Germany, nightime temperatures have fallen below -20 Celsius (minus four Fahrenheit)
Independent U.S. weather forecaster Weather Services Corp (WSC) predicts that temperatures in northwest Europe will remain below normal until the end of the week.
